items.stem: A manager says safety is 'fully delegated to the supervisor'. The problem with this view is that:

options.text: Accountability for safety stays with the manager even when tasks are delegated
options.rationale: Correct: tasks can be delegated but accountability remains with the manager.

options.text: Supervisors cannot be given any tasks
options.rationale: Tasks can be delegated; accountability cannot.

options.text: Safety is not a management concern
options.rationale: Safety is a core management concern.
Responsibility is shared, with manager accountability.

items.explanation: Correct: tasks can be delegated but accountability remains with the manager.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: When controlling a hazard, a manager should reach for personal protective equipment:

options.text: After trying elimination, substitution and engineering controls
options.rationale: Correct: PPE is the last resort in the hierarchy of controls.

options.text: As the very first and only option
options.rationale: PPE is the lowest tier, not the first choice.
Controls are chosen proactively, by the hierarchy.
PPE is permitted as a lower-tier control.

items.explanation: Correct: PPE is the last resort in the hierarchy of controls.

items.stem: Select TWO underlying (root) causes an incident investigation might uncover.

options.rationale: Correct: a training gap is an underlying cause.

options.text: A missing or unenforced safe-work procedure
options.rationale: Correct: a procedure gap is an underlying cause.
'Bad luck' is not an analysable cause.

options.text: The time shown on the clock
options.rationale: Clock time is not a causal factor.

options.text: The colour of the worker's uniform

items.explanation: Correct: a training gap is an underlying cause. Correct: a procedure gap is an underlying cause.
